newsitem.title: CROATIA: $75 million pledged for recovery of Serb enclave.
newsitem.headline: $75 million pledged for recovery of Serb enclave.

text.p: International pledges for the reconstruction of Croatia's last Serb-held enclave rose to $75 million on Friday at a second donors' conference in Zagreb organised by U.N. officials, local media said.

UNTAES, the U.N. Transitional Authority in Eastern Slavonia, estimates rebuilding the region will cost $1.1 billion in all. The Zagreb government says it will be two to three times that amount although it will be able to contribute $1 billion.

Eastern Slavonia, seized by local Serbs in a 1991 revolt against Croatia's move to independence from Yugoslavia, will revert under U.N. supervision to Croatian government rule with minority rights following elections on April 13.
The amount of pledges doubled to $75 million from the $37 million raised at the initial international donors conference held in Croatia in December, the state news agency HINA said.

It said the biggest single donor was the United States with $28 million followed by the 12-nation European Union, Norway and EU members Italy, Germany, Belgium, Austria and the Netherlands with individual pledges.
Russia also promised to contribute, HINA said.
German funds will sponsor growth in enterpreneurship after a half century of Yugoslav communism as well as the removal of land mines from the war-battered region.
Housing, roads and other parts of the infrastructure in a once affluent region wrecked by the 1991 war will be the main targets of reconstruction, U.N. officials said.
UNTAES adviser Didier Fau said reconstruction projects worth $17 million were already under way.

"Our first aim after the elections is the return of refugees and reconstruction which we can't achieve without the help of the international community," said Jacques Klein, a U.S. diplomat in charge of the U.N. mission in the enclave.
"This is a crucial moment for the international community to help Croatia and UNTAES bring its mission to an end."

Croatian Reconstruction Minister Jure Radic thanked all donors for the help given but stressed it remained far short of what was needed. Other ways to secure help from the world will have to be found, he told the donors.
More than 150 representatives of the Croatian government, local Serb authorities, UNTAES, private aid agencies and foreign embassies attended the donors' conference.
Klein urged Croatia's nationalist government to treat Serb and Croat inhabitants of the region equally when it comes to rebuilding their homes.
UNTAES expects up to 20 percent of the 120,000-odd Serbs in the enclave to flee rather than accept reintegration with Croatia, due to be completed in July.
More than half of the Serb population have obtained Croatian citizenship papers, signalling that they will stay.
